title: Networks
examples: What is the difference between a LAN and a WAN?
Can you explain what a network topology is?
How does a router actually direct data packets?

explain.say: Today we are learning about computer networks. A network connects two or more devices together. These devices can share information and resources easily.

draw.text: Networks connect devices to share resources.

explain.say: A local area network or LAN covers a small physical space. Think about a single school classroom or an office floor. These networks are usually fast and secure.
A wide area network or WAN covers a much larger geographical area. The internet itself is the largest example of a WAN. It connects continents together.
Network topology describes the physical or logical layout of a network. A bus topology uses a single backbone cable for all devices.
Another common topology is the star. In this setup, every device connects directly to a central hub or switch. This makes it very organized.

draw.text: Star Topology: All connect to a central point.

explain.say: Protocols are sets of rules that govern how data is sent. Think of them like a shared language for computers to understand each other.

faq.q: What is the difference between a LAN and a WAN?
faq.a: A LAN covers a small, limited area like a building. A WAN covers vast areas, connecting different cities or countries.
asks: What scale of area does a WAN cover?

faq.q: What does network topology refer to?
faq.a: It describes the physical or logical arrangement of connections between devices in a network. Common types include bus and star.
asks: How do I know the shape of a network?
What is the layout of a network called?

faq.a: Protocols are essential because they provide a common set of rules. Without them, devices would not know how to interpret incoming data.
asks: What happens if devices don't use the same protocol?

faq.q: What is the role of the TCP/IP layers?
faq.a: These layers structure how data moves from source to destination. They break down complex communication into manageable steps for reliable transfer.
asks: How is data packaged for the internet?
What is the function of the different layers?

faq.a: A router examines the destination address of a data packet. It then uses routing tables to determine the best next hop toward that destination.
asks: Does a router just pass data along?
What information does a router look at?

facts: LANs are typically used within a single organization or campus.
The internet is the largest example of a Wide Area Network.
The star topology connects all nodes to a central point.
Protocols define the rules for data exchange between devices.

quiz.say: A network connecting all computers in a single university building is most likely a:
quiz.why: A university building represents a small, contained physical area suitable for a LAN.

wrong.1: A WAN covers much larger areas, like connecting different cities.
wrong.2: Bus describes the physical shape, not the size of the network.
wrong.3: A protocol is a set of rules, not a type of network.

quiz.say: If every device connects directly to a central switch, what topology is used?
quiz.why: The description of connecting everything to a central point matches the star topology.

wrong.0: Mesh connects every device to many other devices.
wrong.2: Bus uses one main cable running through all devices.
wrong.3: Ring connects devices in a closed loop or circle.

quiz.say: When data travels across the internet, which component directs it to the next best network?
quiz.why: Routers are specifically designed to read addresses and forward data between different networks.

wrong.0: A switch usually manages traffic only within one local network segment.
wrong.1: A hub simply broadcasts data to every connected device.
wrong.2: A protocol is the rule set, not the physical directing device.
